lens: Every printed number re-derived from research/manuscripts/fusion-partner/emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json at the same pin, independently of its generator: Wilson 95% score intervals recomputed from raw {events,denom}; Fisher exact two-sided p-values recomputed by exhaustive hypergeometric enumeration; every arm gap recomputed; every pooled total checked against the per-cohort parts it is a total of; denominator conventions checked against analyses.C_partner_prevalence.denominator_convention and against each cohort's counts/not_partner_assigned; every multi-site figure enumerated by grep across the whole document rather than assumed consistent; arm assignment checked cell by cell against cohorts[*].strata. Also re-ran research/manuscripts/emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py at the pin and diffed its output against the committed artifact.
central_claim: Arithmetically the paper is in very good shape: all 44 Wilson percent/interval blocks and all 14 contrast blocks in the artifact recompute exactly from their own integer counts, the generator reproduces the committed artifact byte-identically apart from _generated_utc, every one of the 30 in-prose 'a/b = x %' fractions and 11 in-prose Wilson intervals matches, every pooled total equals the parts it is a total of, and no arm is swapped at any of the ~40 sites where an arm-labelled figure appears. The two defects are not transcription errors — they are (1) a retracted prevalence claim that survives at a site Appendix A30's own four-site list does not cover, and (2) a falsifier whose stated arithmetic consequence does not follow from the counts it names.

blockers.where: §1.3 · What this synthesis adds (line 131 of the pinned file)
blockers.quote: It also surfaces five things that no individual source says out loud: ... a prevalence figure materially below the one the field repeats; and an attribution correction to the field's most-quoted caveat (§3.8).
blockers.why_wrong: This is the exact claim Appendix A30 retracts, still asserted as live text. A30 names its live sites as 'the Abstract, §3.5, the §5 claims bullet and, as an attribution, A3 above — four sites in this document', and all four were repaired; §1.3 is a FIFTH site and was not. The retraction survives at §1.3 because the sentence carries no numeral ('materially below the one the field repeats' rather than 'below the ≈27 %'), so neither A30's site list nor the prose guard's `≈27 %` census could see it. The artifact establishes the opposite of what §1.3 tells the reader: the pooled TAF15 share is 28/154 = 18.2 % (95 % CI 12.9–25.0) and the only general TAF15 share this document's own reference list states is ≈20 %, which is INSIDE that interval. §3.5 says so in terms — 'This pooling therefore does not correct that figure' — so a reader meeting §1.3 first is told the paper corrects the field downward, and a reader meeting §3.5 is told it does not.
blockers.evidence: emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → analyses.C_partner_prevalence.external_reported_share.percent_approx = 20; .pooled_percent_for_comparison = 18.2; .pooled_ci95_for_comparison = [12.9, 25.0]; .falls_inside_pooled_interval = true; .reading = 'The share the cited literature states falls INSIDE the interval this pooling computes, so the pooling is consistent with it.' And analyses.C_partner_prevalence.outlier_note: 'NO SOURCE FOR THAT QUOTING PRACTICE WAS EVER HELD ... The pooling is consistent with the cited literature and its contribution is the interval, not a correction of a point figure.' Re-derived independently: Wilson(28,154) = 18.2 % (12.9–25.0), and 20 ∈ [12.9, 25.0].

blockers.where: §6 · What would falsify this, falsifier #5 (and its one home, what_could_kill_this[4])
blockers.quote: A **third** outcome cohort with per-partner event counts in which TAF15 mortality is not elevated. The pooled crude death contrast rests on two TAF15 arms of 7 and 8 patients; a third of similar size disagreeing would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval.
blockers.why_wrong: The arithmetic consequence does not follow from the counts the sentence itself names. The pooled TAF15 arm is 7/15 = 46.7 %; the comparator arm's 95 % Wilson interval is 4.8–20.8 % (both printed in §3.3's own table). A third cohort 'of similar size' means a TAF15 arm of 7 or 8. The most favourable possible case — 0 deaths in 8 TAF15 patients — gives a pooled point estimate of 7/23 = 30.4 %, which is 9.6 points ABOVE the comparator arm's upper bound, not inside it; 0/7 gives 7/22 = 31.8 %. Letting the comparator arm grow with the third cohort makes it worse, not better: a Huang-shaped third cohort adding 42 EWSR1 with 5 deaths gives a comparator of 11/100 = 11.0 % (95 % CI 6.3–18.6), and 30.4 % is still outside. Solving for what would actually be needed: 7/(15+n) ≤ 20.8 % requires n ≥ 19 — a third TAF15 arm of at least nineteen patients with ZERO disease-specific deaths, more than twice the size of either existing arm and larger than any TAF15 outcome arm in the paper. As written, falsifier #5 tells a reader the headline is roughly one ordinary-sized cohort away from collapsing; the counts say it is not. The paper's own §6 preamble points at what_could_kill_this as the full list, so this is the sentence a reader would act on when judging fragility.
blockers.evidence: emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → what_could_kill_this[4] (identical wording); analyses.B_outcome_by_partner.disease_specific_death.taf15_arm = {events 7, denom 15, percent 46.7} and .comparator_arm = {events 6, denom 58, percent 10.3, ci95_lo_percent 4.8, ci95_hi_percent 20.8}; per_cohort TAF15 denoms 7 (agaram-2014-outcome) and 8 (huang-2023-outcome). Recomputed: Wilson(7,23) = 30.4 % (15.6–50.9); Wilson(7,22) = 31.8 % (16.4–52.7); Wilson(11,100) = 11.0 % (6.3–18.6); Wilson(6,100) = 6.0 % (2.8–12.5); smallest n with 7/(15+n) ≤ 20.8 is n = 19 (7/34 = 20.6 %).

p1s.where: §1.2 · Four literatures that had never been combined — the 'Partner prevalence' row, 'what it does not do' cell
p1s.quote: never pooled across series; the field quotes one cohort
p1s.why_wrong: A second live residue of the same A30 retraction, and it is the same numberless shape as ARITH-B1. A30's finding is that no source for any quoting practice was ever held anywhere in this repository; §3.5 restates that in its own superseded note ('no source for that quoting practice was ever held here'). §1.2 nonetheless still tells the reader, as fact, what the field quotes and from where. Correct-looking now only because no number is attached, and nothing binds it: the prose guard keys the retraction on the literal `≈27 %` and on 'below the (\d+\.\d) % of the single referral-centre series', neither of which this cell contains. A reviewer may reasonably grade this a blocker alongside B1; it is graded P1 here because it makes no quantitative comparison of its own.
p1s.evidence: emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → analyses.C_partner_prevalence.outlier_note ('NO SOURCE FOR THAT QUOTING PRACTICE WAS EVER HELD'); Appendix A30's site list names four sites and not this one; research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED row for r'≈27 %' asserting 'The claim is retracted at all four of its live sites'.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py — the A30 bindings (bind() on r'below the (\d+\.\d) % of the single referral-centre series' and the r'≈27 %' declaration row)
p1s.quote: The claim is retracted at all four of its live sites; the string survives only inside retained `Superseded, retained` quotations and the A3/A30 appendix rows.
p1s.why_wrong: The guard that is supposed to hold the A30 retraction down is keyed entirely on numerals — the `≈27 %` string and the '(\d+\.\d) % of the single referral-centre series' construction. A restatement of the retracted claim that carries no numeral is bound by nothing, which is exactly how ARITH-B1 and ARITH-P1-1 survived a round that believed it had closed the class. Coverage gap, P1 by construction: an ordinary future edit that paraphrases 'the field quotes X' without a figure re-opens the defect silently, and the round-7 harness reports 46/46 mutations caught on a mutation set drawn only from numeral-bearing sites.
p1s.evidence: test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py lines ~954–996 and the DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED entry at ~1468; §1.3 and §1.2's cells contain the claim and no numeral, and the committed guard passes on the pinned tree.

p1s.quote: a third of similar size disagreeing would put the pooled point estimate inside the comparator arm's interval
p1s.why_wrong: This is a hand-typed quantitative consequence of numbers the same file computes, and nothing re-derives it. Every other quantitative claim in the artifact goes through wilson()/contrast()/_stratum_extent(); this one is prose in a list of strings, so it drifted out of agreement with the counts (ARITH-B2) with no symptom. It is the same defect class the file already closed twice — method.not_used's stratum extent (now derived by _stratum_extent) and §8's own record counts (now derived by the prose guard) — left open at a third site. The falsifier's arithmetic is computable in one line from the two arms it names, so the fix is a derivation, not a re-typing.
p1s.evidence: emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py _stratum_extent() docstring ('a total is DERIVED, never typed — so it is derived, and the class of defect is closed rather than the instance') against what_could_kill_this, which is a literal list of strings; Appendix A20's identical finding for §8's counts.

p1s.where: §2.5 · Methods deliberately not used — the I² bullet, against §3.5's prevalence table
p1s.quote: the range of per-cohort rates, printed beside every pooled figure — §3.1 for the TKI-response secondary pool, §3.3 for each of the three outcome rows, §3.5 for prevalence — and computed in the artifact's `heterogeneity` blocks, which are the one home of every one of these spreads.
p1s.why_wrong: Three of the four pooled figures in §3.5's table — EWSR1 120/154 = 77.9 %, TCF12 5/154 = 3.2 %, TFG 1/154 = 0.6 % — carry no per-cohort range in the prose, and the artifact carries no heterogeneity block for them either: analyses.C_partner_prevalence has heterogeneity_TAF15 and nothing else. The universality clause is therefore still measurably over-broad inside the document, which is exactly what Appendix A22 corrected once already (for the secondary TKI pool and the local-recurrence comparator arm) with 'the fix prints them rather than softening the rule'. It is graded P1 rather than blocker because the enumeration that follows the clause scopes it to '§3.5 for prevalence' as a locator; an ordinary edit — quoting the EWSR1 share, or adding a fifth prevalence series — lands on a spread that neither the prose nor the artifact holds, and nothing catches it.
p1s.evidence: emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → analyses.C_partner_prevalence: keys are pooled, heterogeneity_TAF15, external_reported_share, context_range_note, outlier_note, verdict; there is no heterogeneity_EWSR1 / _TCF12 / _TFG. §3.5's table prints CIs for all four rows and a per-cohort range for TAF15 only ('Per-cohort TAF15 share ranges 15.8 – 29.2 % (spread 13.4 points)').

p2s.where: Abstract and §3.3 table — the disease-specific-death gap
p2s.why_wrong: 46.7 − 10.3 = 36.4, not 36.3. The artifact is right and the presentation is what misleads: contrast() subtracts the exact proportions and rounds once (6/58 − 7/15 = −0.36322 → −36.3), while the two percentages printed immediately beside the gap are each rounded first. A reader re-deriving the paper's single most quotable number from the two figures next to it gets a different answer. The other two rows happen not to show it (4.3 and 9.2 agree either way). Fix is a footnote on the convention, not a changed number.
p2s.evidence: emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py contrast(): round(100 * (other['events']/other['denom'] − taf['events']/taf['denom']), 1); artifact comparator_minus_taf15_percentage_points = −36.3 for dod_pooled_agaram2014_huang2023; recomputed exact difference −36.3218 %, recomputed difference-of-rounded-percents −36.4.

p2s.where: §3.2 and §3.3 ('23 partner-assigned with follow-up') against §3.5 ('Agaram 2014 (24 assigned)')
p2s.quote: Agaram 2014 (MSKCC, 26 consecutive cases, 23 partner-assigned with follow-up)
p2s.why_wrong: The same cohort is given two different 'partner-assigned' counts under the same word, and the clause that appears to explain the difference is not the one that causes it. Agaram has 24 partner-assigned cases (EWSR1 16 + TAF15 7 + TCF12 1) and follow-up in all 26; the outcome pool's 23 is EWSR1 + TAF15 only, i.e. the TCF12 case is dropped because it is not in either arm, not because it lacks follow-up. A reader reconciling 24 against 23 will conclude one Agaram case was lost to follow-up, which the record contradicts. Same convention collision on Huang: 57 partner-assigned in §3.5 versus '50 partner-assigned with follow-up of 58' in §3.2, where the 7 lost are 2 TCF12 plus 5 without follow-up. The artifact itself is unambiguous — its verdict says '73 patients with an assigned EWSR1 or TAF15 partner and follow-up' — and the prose drops the 'EWSR1 or TAF15' qualifier that does the work.
p2s.evidence: emc-fusion-partner-pooling.json → analyses.C_partner_prevalence.denominator_convention ('Partner-assigned cases only'); partner_assigned_per_cohort['agaram-2014-prevalence'] = 24; cohorts[agaram-2014-prevalence].counts = {EWSR1 16, TAF15 7, TCF12 1}; citations.agaram2014.population = 'follow-up available in all 26 (2-99 months)'; analyses.B_outcome_by_partner.verdict.

p2s.quote: Agaram's arms differ about two-fold in mean follow-up (21.7 vs 43.3 months, biasing *against* the TAF15 arm accruing events)
p2s.why_wrong: The pair is printed in opposite orders at the two sites and neither site labels which arm is which, so at most one of them can be read correctly by a reader assuming a consistent convention. The record is unambiguous — EWSR1 43.3, TAF15 21.7 — and §3.3's order happens to match the table's TAF15-first column order while §4.7's does not. Neither figure is wrong; the arm attachment is simply unstated at both. The artifact reproduces the same inconsistency between follow_up_caveat and cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning, so the fix belongs in the generator too.
p2s.evidence: cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].strata['EWSR1::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 43.3 and ['TAF15::NR4A3'].mean_followup_months = 21.7; analyses.B_outcome_by_partner.follow_up_caveat prints '(21.7 vs 43.3 months)'; cohorts[agaram-2014-outcome].follow_up_warning prints '(43.3 vs 21.7 months)'.

p2s.quote: every TAF15 arm carrying an actual outcome is 2–8 patients — the pooled TAF15 outcome arm is 15
p2s.why_wrong: The same paragraph's retained superseded note names Paioli 2021's TAF15 group of 10, and Paioli does report an outcome for it (DFS p = 0.08, DMFS p = 0.09 by partner) — what it does not publish is event counts. So '2–8' is true of every TAF15 arm with integer event counts and false of every TAF15 arm carrying an outcome. One word ('counts') fixes it; as written the range understates the largest TAF15 group the paper actually discusses.
p2s.evidence: cohorts[paioli-2021-prevalence].counts['TAF15::NR4A3'] = 10; cohorts[paioli-2021-outcome].published_p_values = {disease_free_survival_by_partner 0.08, distant_metastasis_free_survival_by_partner 0.09} with contextReason 'counts-not-reported'; §4.1's own retained note: 'The only larger TAF15 groups (Huang 2023's 9, Paioli 2021's 10) publish no event counts at all ... Paioli 2021's clause stands.'

what_you_could_not_break: Almost all of it, and the failures were exhaustive rather than sampled. (1) All 44 blocks in the artifact carrying {events, denom, percent, ci95_lo_percent, ci95_hi_percent} recompute exactly from their own integers under an independently written Wilson score interval at z = 1.959964 — zero mismatches, including every zero-event arm. (2) All 14 TAF15-vs-comparator contrasts reproduce their Fisher exact two-sided p under an independently written exhaustive hypergeometric enumeration: 1.0, 0.155, 0.0034, 0.7389, 0.5163, 0.6974, 1.0, 0.0672, 0.2095, 1.0, 0.0264, 1.0, 0.3506 and the sensitivity arm — zero mismatches. (3) All 30 'a/b = x %' fractions printed in the prose recompute; all 11 Wilson intervals printed in the prose recompute. (4) Every pooled total equals its parts: disease-specific death 3/7 + 4/8 = 7/15 and 1/16 + 5/42 = 6/58; local recurrence 2/7 + 2/8 = 4/15 and 1/16 + 12/42 = 13/58; distant metastasis 2/7 + 3/8 = 5/15 and 6/16 + 8/42 = 14/58; TKI secondary 0/2 + 0/3 = 0/5 and 6/8 + 4/19 = 10/27; prevalence 16+46+8+50 = 120, 7+9+2+10 = 28, 1+2+1+1 = 5, 1 = 1, summing to 154 with per-cohort assigned totals 24+57+11+62 = 154 and residues 2, 1, 1, 5 each equal to n_tested minus assigned. Huang's three-way partitions close exactly (4+0+4 = 8, 5+12+25 = 42; 1+3 = 4 and 8+8 = 16). The counterfactual 28+3 = 31 over 154+9 = 163 = 19.0 % reproduces. (5) No arm is swapped anywhere: every arm-labelled figure in §3.1, §3.3, §3.4 and §3.5 attaches to the cohort and partner the artifact's strata assign it to, including the two places most exposed to it — Agaram's metastasis reversal (EWSR1 6/16 higher, TAF15 2/7 lower) and Huang's counter-direction (EWSR1 8/42, TAF15 3/8). (6) Multi-site consistency: every one of 46.7, 10.3, 36.3, 0.0034, 7/15, 6/58, 18.2, 12.9–25.0, 43.4, 56.1, 21.1, 37.0, 29.2, 24.8–69.9, 53.9, 22.4, 13.4, 9.2, 4.3, 31/163, 78 %, HR 30.60 and HR 8.14 is identical at every site it appears (enumerated by grep, 4 to 8 sites each). (7) §8's self-counts are exact: 17 citation records, 13 with a verification_note, exactly 4 of those (stacchiotti2014, stacchiotti2019, huang2023, sjogren2003) naming both a cache slug and an HTTP status — suemitsu2025 names a status but no slug, so the count is right and so is the enumeration — 16 cohort records none of which carries verified/verification_note/cache_path/http_status, zero occurrences of cache_path or http_status as field names anywhere in the artifact, and 9 entries in retrieval_provenance.cache_slugs_used. (8) §3.5's 'complete author lists — 5, 20, 18 and 16 names' is exactly right and the four lists intersect in nobody. (9) §2.5's derived stratum extent (denominators 3 to 58, events 0 to 14) is correct over the ten strata the sentence names, and I confirmed the generator's deliberate refusal to compute it by recursive walk was the right call — a walk returns 2–58 / 0–16. (10) §3.6's GSE28866 ratios reproduce from the other artifact at the same pin: 0.53475/0.29422 = 1.82 → 1.8×, 0.53475/0.32171 = 1.66 → 1.7×, n = 4 EMC libraries. (11) §3.4's recording of Huang's internal size-row inconsistency is itself correct: 12/46 = 26.1 %, 12/43 = 27.9 %, 13/46 = 28.3 %, 7/9 = 77.8 %. (12) §7's reproducibility claim holds at the pin — re-running emc_fusion_partner_pooling.py produced an object identical to the committed artifact in every key except _generated_utc. (13) Every one of the 15 reference entries matches its artifact citation record on journal, year, PMID, PMCID and DOI.
could_not_check: Whether the integers in the generator's COHORTS table are the integers the source documents actually print. Everything here is internal consistency — prose against artifact against independent recomputation — and no source was opened. The one count set the paper itself flags as human-transcribed (Huang 2023 Table 1) is exactly the one an arithmetic seat cannot reach: it is not in the literature cache, the publisher's edge 403s automation, and §4.7a already discloses this.

Huang 2023's own '12/46 (28 %)' discrepancy. The paper records it without resolving it, which is the correct move under POLICY-evidence.md §2.1(2); which of the three printed numbers is wrong is only decidable from the PDF.

Whether analyses.A_tki_objective_response's held-out sunitinib series really is non-overlapping with the trial. This is a pooling decision, not arithmetic, and the paper states both analyses; I checked only that both reproduce from their stated counts.

The GSE28866 upstream 3SEQ peak processing behind the 1.8×/1.7× SEMA3C ratios. I re-derived the ratios from that artifact's per_gene.values medians; I did not re-run the read-density pipeline that produced the medians.
